name: m4-typecomparer-class-typer-kperf
description: Does moving `TypeComparers`' logic into a final class, `TypeComparer`, pay on a typer-only compile of the scala corpus? Its private methods were `invokespecial`s on the `TypeComparers` interface, each with a C2 receiver check against it; on a base with a 70-entry `Global` those checks were 3% of cycles in `lookup_secondary_supers_table_slow_path_stub`. On `2.13.x`, after [scala/scala#11365](https://github.com/scala/scala/pull/11365), `Global` has 52 and the check is a hashed lookup.
One fork per build and round, kperf cycles and instructions, JIT recorded over each whole fork. Patched JDK 26, `SCALA_RELEASE_OPT`.

variantDescriptions.tc: `base` + [retronym/scala#208](https://github.com/retronym/scala/pull/208) + the `isHigherKinded` prototype + `TypeComparers`' logic in a final class, `TypeComparer` (`58d0363519`)
